title: How and why questions review
focus: Ask about manner, degree and reasons, and give the corresponding information answers.
targetSkills: Miten and kuinka: answering about manner
Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree

exercises.prompt: Write “How does he read?” in Finnish. Use hän (“he or she”), lukee (“reads”).
exercises.explanation: A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. Miten asks how something happens. Kuinka can ask about manner too in these examples, although the two words are not interchangeable in every Finnish expression. The complete question means “How does he read”.
requiredSkills: Miten and kuinka: answering about manner
exercises.targetSkill: Miten and kuinka: answering about manner

parts.role: question asking how the action happens
parts.formation: Miten asks about manner or method in these examples.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Hän refers to one other person without specifying gender.
Use the strong stem luke- and lengthen final e: lukee.

optionFeedback.Miten hän lukee?: A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. Miten asks how something happens. Kuinka can ask about manner too in these examples, although the two words are not interchangeable in every Finnish expression. The complete question means “How does he read”.
optionFeedback.Missä hän lukee?: This form asks for a different relationship or gives a location instead of the requested source. Match the complete intended meaning.
optionFeedback.Miksi hän lukee?: Choose the question word for the requested information; keep the complete intended meaning.

exercises.explanation: A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. Answer with a manner word, often an adverb, which tells how an action happens: hyvin (“well”), hitaasti (“slowly”), nopeasti (“quickly”) or selvästi (“clearly”). The adjective describing a person and the adverb describing an action are different: hidas (“slow”) becomes hitaasti (“slowly”), with the weak d changing to t in this stem. The complete reply means “He reads clearly”.

exercises.prompt: Write “How long is the journey?” in Finnish. Use matka (“journey”), on (“is”), pitkä (“tall or long”).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. An adjective is a word that describes a quality. Kuinka before an adjective asks about degree: Kuinka vanha olet? (“How old are you?”) and Kuinka pitkä matka on? (“How long is the journey?”). Miten is possible in several such patterns; these tasks teach the neutral kuinka pattern and accept a natural miten alternative. The complete question means “How long is the journey”.
requiredSkills: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree
exercises.targetSkill: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking the degree of a quality + quality whose degree is being asked about + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.role: question asking the degree of a quality
parts.formation: Kuinka asks about manner or, before an adjective, degree.

parts.role: quality whose degree is being asked about
parts.formation: Pitkä describes a person's height or a thing's length; context determines tall or long.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Matka is the basic noun meaning journey; its length can answer kuinka pitkä.
Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Miksi asks for a reason: why. The requested question is “Kuinka pitkä matka on?”

exercises.prompt: Build “The journey is three kilometres long.” in Finnish.
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. Give the requested age or measurement, using the provided complete expression. Olen kaksikymmentä vuotta vanha means I am twenty years old. Matka on kaksi kilometriä means the journey is two kilometres long. Another age pattern uses -vuotias, but its formation is outside this bounded target. The complete reply means “The journey is three kilometres long”.
requiredSkills: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree
exercises.targetSkill: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree

sentenceExplanation.translation: The journey is three kilometres long.

parts.formation: Matka is the basic noun meaning journey; its length can answer kuinka pitkä.
Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.
Kolme is the supplied number three.
Kilometri + -ä gives singular partitive kilometriä after a number greater than one.

exercises.prompt: Complete “Why are you going home?”: ____ sinä menet kotiin? Write the full sentence. Use kotiin (“home”), menet (“you go”), sinä (“you”). Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Miksi asks why. Koska introduces the reason in the answer: Miksi olet kotona? — Koska olen sairas (“Why are you at home? — Because I am ill”). The complete question means “Why are you going home”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking for a reason + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state) + destination

parts.formation: Miksi asks for a reason.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Sinä addresses one person informally.
Mene- + singular second-person -t gives menet.
Koti repeats final i and adds n: kotiin means towards home.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Miten asks how something happens. The requested question is “Miksi sinä menet kotiin?”

exercises.prompt: Build “Because I am tired.” in Finnish.
exercises.explanation: A koska-clause is a natural short answer to miksi. Put koska before an ordinary statement with its person and verb. A full answer can repeat the main situation before the because-clause. Here the supporting clauses are provided, so the new decision is reason versus question. The complete reply means “Because I am tired”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: connector introducing the reason + verb (the action or state) + description of what the subject is like

parts.formation: Koska introduces the reason clause in these replies.
Olla has the I-form olen: ole- + -n. The ending identifies the speaker.

parts.role: description of what the subject is like
parts.formation: Väsynyt is a describing word meaning tired in these sentences.
